name: Goa Carnival
description: Goa's largest carnival parade, with Margao hosting vibrant celebrations on February 15. The parade moves from Holy Spirit Church to Margao Municipal Council Square, featuring elaborate floats, dance groups, drummers, and live music in South Goa's main city.
significance: Christian cultural festival celebrating pre-Lenten traditions

name: Shigmo (Shigmotsav)
description: Goa's major spring harvest festival with large parade in Margao on March 14. Hundreds of folk artists perform traditional dances like Ghode Mhodni and Romtamel while massive Chitrarath floats depicting scenes from Hindu epics roll through the city centre.
significance: Hindu spring festival rooted in Phalguna month, celebrating harvest and renewal

name: Goa Carnival
description: While Candolim beach itself is not a primary carnival parade site, it is near Panaji which hosts the main and most vibrant Goa Carnival parade on February 14, making it accessible for visitors staying in this North Goa beach area.
significance: Christian cultural festival celebrating pre-Lenten traditions

name: Feast of the Three Kings (Reis Magos)
description: The Chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Remédios (Our Lady of Cures), also known as the Three Kings Chapel, atop the Cuelim hillock near Reis Magos, hosts the most famous celebration. Three young boys enact the role of the Three Kings, traveling on horseback through different paths and converging near the chapel.
significance: Christian religious festival commemorating the visit of the Three Wise Men to Bethlehem

name: Sao Joao Festival (São João)
description: Siolim hosts a distinctive 175-year-old boat festival tradition where revellers from surrounding villages (Chapora, Zhor, Badem, Assagao) arrive in beautifully decorated boats to pay homage at the Chapel of São João in Pereira Vaddo. Boats are decorated with flowers, leaves, and designs of guitars, birds, fruit baskets, sea creatures, and mythical creatures. Festival begins at 3:30 PM with boats arriving between 4 PM and 5:30 PM.
significance: Catholic religious festival celebrating St. John the Baptist, merged with monsoon and community traditions

name: Sao Joao Festival (São João)
description: Sao Joao is celebrated across North Goa, with significant traditions in Assagao. Revellers from Badem in Assagao join other villages in the famous boat procession to Siolim's Chapel of São João, connecting Assagao's Catholic heritage with this major monsoon celebration.
significance: Catholic religious festival celebrating St. John the Baptist, merged with monsoon and community traditions

name: Shigmo (Shigmotsav)
description: Ponda marks the official start of Shigmotsav on March 5, 2026. Local Hindu temples including Shantadurga Temple, Mangeshi Temple (in nearby Priol), and Mahalsa Temple (in Mardol) host celebrations with folk artists performing traditional dances and farmers gathering for rituals, folk songs, and community feasts.
significance: Hindu spring festival rooted in Phalguna month, celebrating harvest and renewal with temple-centered traditions

name: Shantadurga Temple Annual Fair
description: The Shri Shantadurga Temple in Ponda, an 18th-century sanctuary dedicated to Goddess Durga, hosts an annual fair during December-January. The temple exhibits Indo-Portuguese architectural styles and is a major spiritual landmark in central Goa's Hindu heartland.
significance: Hindu religious festival at a major goddess temple celebrating devotional traditions

name: Mahalsa Temple Annual Jatra
description: The Shri Mahalsa Narayani Temple in Mardol, near Ponda, hosts an annual Jatra (festival) dedicated to Goddess Mahalasa (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu). The celebration features elaborate rituals, cultural programs, and processions that draw crowds from various parts of Goa.
significance: Hindu religious festival celebrating goddess traditions with community processions

name: Goa Sea Turtle Festival
description: Morjim hosts the Goa Sea Turtle Festival to celebrate the annual olive ridley turtle nesting season. The beach is one of Goa's four major turtle nesting sites. Festival features educational workshops about sea turtles, conservation efforts, and responsible citizen behaviour, with events like coastal trails to watch sea birds and understand sand dune ecology.
significance: Conservation and environmental awareness festival celebrating marine life and ocean ecosystems

name: Goa Sea Turtle Festival
description: Agonda is one of Goa's four major olive ridley turtle nesting sites and participates in the statewide Goa Sea Turtle Festival. Educational workshops and conservation activities are held during the nesting season to raise awareness about sea turtle habitats and protection efforts.
significance: Conservation and environmental awareness festival celebrating marine life and ocean ecosystems

name: Goa Sea Turtle Festival
description: Mandrem is one of Goa's four major olive ridley turtle nesting sites and participates in the statewide Goa Sea Turtle Festival. The beach hosts educational workshops and conservation activities during the turtle nesting season to raise awareness and celebrate this important marine habitat.
significance: Conservation and environmental awareness festival celebrating marine life and ocean ecosystems
